Landed. ModelFormula(onset: ColumnId), ArgValue.Ident(ColumnId), and id/prefix/label as TermId. FormulaParser is the lifting boundary: the tokenizer's isIdentStart/isIdentPart already guarantee everything ColumnId requires, so the lift is ColumnId.unsafe at exactly one place in parsePrimary — the token has been parsed by the time it gets there. A TermId from a string literal can genuinely fail, so TermArgs.termId reports it as a ParseError with the usual character offset.

One departure from the bead, and it removes rather than adds: contrasts was retyped from Option[ArgValue] to Option[String], on the same reasoning this bead applies to basis — it keys the user-extensible contrast-set registry, so an open set is right. That was the single identifier position where ColumnId would have been a lie (a contrast set is never a column), and typing it deleted contrastSetKeyEither and an unreachable FormulaBinding branch. hrf_fun stays an ArgValue because an Ident there is genuinely column-or-key: the registry is tried first, then a column of HRFs.

Downstream cost was as measured — AnalysisSpec.scala, plus its two now-dead checks: require(formula.onset.trim.nonEmpty) and the matching branch in ModelRecipe.make are gone, because with onset: ColumnId that is a property of the type.

design 157 tests, JVM+JS green.
